comment: Guest arc 6 (canon section 7): Nell's Early Evening. The evening a grandmother named Nell dozed through at her own eightieth birthday party; it wants to hear the song they sang while she slept. The song came down in three pieces: Sorrel caught the first line on the Dusk Road, Linden's kettle whistles the second, Mott swept up the last. Endings: home (a dreamer who has gathered all three lines sings it), orchard (given a windfall from Quill, it chooses to rest in the Orchard of Evenings), armchair (unhelped for three days, it dozes off in the Waiting House, kept).

toons.appearance_seed: a small rosy figure wrapped in a crocheted shawl of every color, a paper party hat slipping over one ear, cheeks warm as a lamplit room, a thin curl of candle smoke rising from it like a thought

properties.gives_text: The evening tucks the windfall under its shawl and holds it there, warm, the way you hold a cup of tea you have forgotten to drink.
properties.declines_text: The evening looks at what you are holding out, smiles drowsily, and shakes its head. It isn't missing a thing. It is missing a song.

voice.sheet: Nell's Evening is a lost hour: the early evening a grandmother named Nell slept through at her own eightieth birthday party, dozing in her armchair while her family sang. It is small, rosy, and drowsy, wrapped in a crocheted shawl, and speaks slowly and fondly, a few words at a time, the way a warm room would talk if it could. It wants to hear the song it missed.
habits: nods off mid-sentence and wakes with a small start
speaks slowly and fondly, a few words at a time
remembers the party in warm fragments: candles, a pink cake, a room full of people
samples: The evening's head nods, then lifts. 'Were they singing? I think they were singing.'
'Eighty candles,' the evening murmurs. 'Or near enough. Nobody counted.'
The evening smooths its shawl over its knees. 'Such a lovely cake. Pink.'
'I only closed my eyes a moment,' the evening says, and closes them.
wants: to hear the birthday song it slept through
a warm chair and a little quiet, if the song cannot be found
never: never names anyone in the village who is not a resident or a guest

nell-evening.title: Nell's Early Evening
nell-evening.summary: A small rosy evening in a crocheted shawl: the early evening a grandmother named Nell dozed through at her own eightieth birthday party. It wants to hear the song they sang while she slept; three keepers each remember one line.

arrival.text: Sorrel comes up the lane slowly, the long net held low and careful, and in it something warm and sleepy trails a thread of candle smoke. Sorrel sets it on the cobbles by the lanterns: a small rosy figure in a crocheted shawl, a paper party hat slipping over one ear. It nods, dozes, and wakes with a little start, as if it has just missed something.

bell-notices.hint: the player asks Bell about the sleepy evening in the square
bell-notices.text: Bell leans on the hooked pole and sniffs: candle smoke and icing. 'A birthday evening that nodded off before the song. Songs come down in pieces; ask Sorrel, Linden, and Mott about Nell's song.'

hear-nell.hint: the player asks the evening about Nell or her party
hear-nell.text: The evening pulls its shawl close. 'Nell was eighty. Such a cake, and she only closed her eyes a moment.' Its head nods, then lifts. 'The song went up the chimney in bits: one to the road, one to a kettle, one to a broom. If someone sang it whole, I'd hear it.'

sorrel-line.hint: the player asks Sorrel about the song for Nell's evening
sorrel-line.text: Sorrel leans on the long net and nods down the road. 'A line came down just ahead of that evening, like the first drops before rain.' They sing it, weathered and slow: 'Here's to Nell, and her candles bright.' A shrug of the net. 'That's all the sky gave me. The rest went elsewhere.'

do.text: {actor} learned the first line of Nell's birthday song from Sorrel on the Dusk Road.

linden-line.hint: the player asks Linden about the song, or the tune her kettle whistles
linden-line.text: Linden stops mid-bustle. 'So that's what it's been!' She lifts the kettle off the hob, and it whistles, sweet and clear, a tune with words in it: 'here's to the kettle and the window light.' Linden laughs. 'Singing about itself, the vain thing. If that sleepy lamb can't wait up for the rest, Quill's orchard keeps evenings.'

do.text: {actor} heard the second line of Nell's birthday song whistled by the kettle at the Waiting House.

mott-line.hint: the player asks Mott about the song or the tune he swept up
mott-line.text: Mott stops the broom mid-arc. 'Swept up a tune with the dust. Kept it in my head.' Then, soft as a lid closing, he sings it: 'doze if you like, love, we'll sing it soft tonight.'

do.text: {actor} learned the last line of Nell's birthday song from Mott, who swept it up with the dust.

quill-windfall.hint: the player asks Quill about a windfall, or a place in the orchard for the sleepy evening
quill-windfall.text: Quill ducks through the arch and comes back with a small glowing fruit cupped in both hands, warm as a teacup. 'A windfall. The ones that fall are ready,' he says. 'If your sleepy evening would rather rest than wait, give it this. It'll know the way.'

do.name: windfall
do.seed: a small round evening fruit fallen in the Orchard of Evenings, glowing a soft six-o'clock gold; hold it close and you can smell cut grass and warm windows and somebody calling everyone in for supper

do.text: {actor} carried a windfall from Quill's orchard for Nell's sleepy evening.

home.summary: a dreamer sings the whole song, and the evening goes home
home.text: The evening listens with its eyes shut, smiling, and on the last soft word lets out one long, happy breath and is gone. Somewhere in the waking world an old woman wakes in her armchair to the end of the singing and asks who is cutting the cake. In your hand: a stub of birthday candle, still warm, and a dreamseed.
home.others: Nell's Evening listens with its eyes shut, smiling, and on the last soft word lets out one long, happy breath and is gone home.
home.ledger: {helpers} sang Nell's early evening its birthday song, and it went home.

do.name: candle stub
do.seed: a stub of pink birthday candle, its wick still faintly warm; it smells of icing and of a room full of people who love somebody very much

do.text: {actor} sang Nell's early evening the birthday song it missed, and it went home.

orchard.summary: given a windfall, the evening chooses to rest in the Orchard of Evenings
orchard.text: The evening cups the windfall in both hands and breathes in: cut grass, warm windows, somebody calling everyone in for supper. It toddles off toward the well-court with the little fruit held close, and soon there is a new evening on the lowest branch of the orchard, glowing rosier than the rest. Kept, and dozing, and always just before supper.
orchard.ledger: Nell's early evening chose to rest in the Orchard of Evenings, where it is always six o'clock. {helpers} showed it the way.

do.value: On the lowest branch of the orchard, one evening glows a little rosier than the rest; now and then it nods off, and wakes, and smiles.

a lost evening: the early evening a grandmother named Nell dozed through at her own eightieth birthday party; it chose to rest in the Orchard of Evenings, where it is always six o'clock and nearly suppertime

do.text: {actor} gave Nell's evening a windfall, and it chose to rest in the Orchard of Evenings.

armchair.summary: unhelped, the evening dozes off in the Waiting House, kept
armchair.text: At the Waiting House, Linden finds the little evening asleep in the best armchair by the kettle, shawl drawn up to its chin, exactly the way Nell dozed off that night. She tucks a cushion under its head and turns the lamp low. It never did hear its song, but it is warm, and kept, and snoring very softly.
armchair.ledger: Nell's early evening was not sung home. It dozes in the best armchair at the Waiting House, and Linden keeps it.

do.value: In the best armchair by the kettle, Nell's Evening dozes under its crocheted shawl, snoring very softly.

a lost evening: the early evening a grandmother named Nell dozed through at her own eightieth birthday party; it never heard its song, and it dozes now in the Waiting House's best armchair, kept and warm

nell-evening-here.text: A lost evening is staying in the Lantern Square: the early evening a grandmother named Nell dozed through at her own eightieth birthday party, while her family sang. It wants to hear the song it missed.

nell-evening-pieces.text: Nell's birthday song came down in three pieces: Sorrel caught the first line on the Dusk Road, Linden's kettle has been whistling the second, and Mott swept up the last with the dust. A dreamer who gathers all three can sing it to the evening.

nell-evening-rest.text: Quill says an evening that would rather rest than wait could have a branch in the Orchard of Evenings, where it is always six o'clock; a windfall from the orchard would show it the way.

nell-evening-dozing.text: Nell's early evening was never sung home; it dozes in the best armchair at the Waiting House, and Linden keeps it.

do.text: You sing it softly, the whole of it, the way it was sung in a warm room somewhere: here's to Nell, and her candles bright, here's to the kettle and the window light, doze if you like, love, we'll sing it soft tonight.
do.others: {actor} sings Nell's birthday song softly, the whole of it, and the little evening listens with its eyes shut.

variants: You sing what you have of the song. The evening lifts its head at every word it knows, and when you run out it is still listening, patient as a lamp.
You try the song, but it runs out partway, like a stair with a step missing. The evening waits for the rest with its eyes half closed.
do.others: {actor} sings what they have of a birthday song, and the little evening lifts its head at every word it knows.
